deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, March 1813. These are latitude (Polhöhe) determinations with the Reichenbach repeating circle. The previous page gives the March 14 data. The upper half of this page finishes the March 14 reduction of α Ursae minoris observed far from the meridian. The lower half reduces a circum-meridian series of the Cepheus star observed on March 15.

(A) α UMi, March 14, continued.
- On the previous page Gauss writes the identity sin^2(ζ/2) = sin^2((δ−φ)/2) cos^2(h/2) + cos^2((δ+φ)/2) sin^2(h/2). It follows from cos ζ = sinφ sinδ + cosφ cosδ cos h.
- Inputs: assumed φ0 = 51°31'54" and δ = 88°18'41.53". Hence (δ−φ0)/2 = 18°23'23.76" and (δ+φ0)/2 = 69°55'17.76". Then log sin = 9.4989750 and log cos = 9.5356810.
- Four hour angles: h = 134°42'57", 135°43'27", 137°7'27", 139°6'27". The tabulated values are log cos(h/2) and log sin(h/2).
- Row 1 of this page: log a = log[sin((δ−φ)/2) cos(h/2)] = 9.0844056, 9.0752324, 9.0618539, 9.0422090.
- Row 2: log b = log[cos((δ+φ)/2) sin(h/2)] = 9.5008485, 9.5024230, 9.5045440 (written 9.5045449?), 9.5074207 (overwritten).
- Row 3 (implicit step, mine): an auxiliary angle with tan θ = a/b, giving log cos θ = 9.9702313, 9.9715789, 9.9734218, 9.9759005.
- Then sin(ζ/2) = b / cos θ. This is the standard Gaussian addition/subtraction-log device for sqrt(a^2+b^2).
- Column 1 gives log sin(ζ/2) = 9.5306172, so ζ = 39°40'17.9". This agrees with the first listed value.
- Computed zenith distances: 39°40'17.90", 39°41'35.66", 39°43'11.05", 39°45'27.66". Sum 158°50'32.27", mean 39°42'38.07".
- Observed: the repeated arc 158°46'55" divided by 4 gives 39°41'43.75". Adding refraction 51.75" gives 39°42'35.50".
- Equation of condition: 39°42'38.07" − 0.999 dφ = 39°42'35.50". So dφ = +2.57" and φ = 51°31'56.57".
- The coefficient is dζ/dφ = −cos A, where A is the star's azimuth. At the right: log sin p (p ≈ 1°41'18") = 8.46927, plus 0.19456 = −log sin ζ, plus 9.86176 (presumably log sin h), sums to 8.52559. So sin A = 0.03355, A ≈ 1°55' (written '1.55 = Az'), and cos A = 0.9994 ≈ 0.999.
- The marginal column 20.58, 20.30, 19.50, 18.55 is unexplained.

(B) March 15. Clock fast by 6'46.7".
- Star: β Cephei at lower culmination, δ ≈ 69°44'.
- Four pointings at 9h28'35", 32'14", 38'3", 40'53". Repeated arc 234°47'21.25", divided by 4 gives 58°41'50.31".
- Culmination clock time 9h32'56". Time offsets t = 4'21", 0'42", 5'7", 7'57".
- Reduction terms 2 sin^2(t/2)/sin1" = 37.2", 1.0", 51.4", 124.1". Sum 213.7. log 213.7 = 2.32980.
- Factor log[cosφ cosδ / sin(φ+δ)] = 9.40143, taken from the previous page; sin(φ+δ) is used because ζ = 180°−φ−δ at lower culmination. The product is 53.85", divided by 4 gives +13.46". It is additive because the zenith distance is maximal at lower culmination.
- Refraction: log 1.9805 (mean) + 9.9979 (barometer 27z11.3l) + 0.0270 (thermometer −4.75°R) = 2.0054, i.e. 101.25" = 1'41.25".
- Meridian zenith distance: 58°41'50.31" + 1'41.25" + 13.46" = 58°43'45.02".
- φ = 180° − (ζ + δ), with δ = 69°44'18.84". Written result 51°31'56.16"; the arithmetic with 45.02 gives 56.14 (see errors).
errors: Final March 15 latitude: 180° − (58°43'45.02" + 69°44'18.84") = 51°31'56.14", not 56.16". The darker overwritten digits ('13.46', '45.02') show that 13.44 was corrected to 13.46 (53.85/4 = 13.4625) and 45.00 to 45.02. The final line was left as computed from 45.00.
Row 2, column 3: 9.5356810 + 9.9688630 = 9.5045440. The image/transcription reads 9.5045449, a slip of 9 units in the 7th decimal (could be a misreading of a 0).
Row 2, column 4 is overwritten. The correct sum 9.5356810 + 9.9717397 = 9.5074207 matches the '74' reading, not '42'.

The 9.86176 entry in the azimuth computation does not correspond to log sin of any listed hour angle (it gives h ≈ 133°20'; the mean h gives 9.8365). The resulting A ≈ 1°55' differs slightly from ~1°49'. This is immaterial, since only cos A ≈ 0.999 is used.

results.what: Zenith distance of a star at hour angle h from sin^2(ζ/2) = sin^2((δ−φ)/2)cos^2(h/2) + cos^2((δ+φ)/2)sin^2(h/2), evaluated with an auxiliary angle tanθ = a/b, sin(ζ/2) = b/cosθ
results.modern_name: Half-angle form of the spherical cosine rule (astronomical triangle) with auxiliary-angle logarithmic evaluation
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century spherical astronomy (Delambre, Mayer etc.); auxiliary-angle device in common use

results.what: Latitude from off-meridian zenith distances of Polaris via a differential correction ζ_calc − cosA·dφ = ζ_obs
results.modern_name: Latitude by Polaris at any hour angle, linearized equation of condition

results.what: Circum-meridian reduction at lower culmination: Δζ = cosφ cosδ / sin(φ+δ) · mean(2 sin^2(t/2)/sin1")
Refraction as log mean refraction plus barometer and thermometer log corrections

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observatory reductions (Göttingen latitude ≈ 51°31'5x") with a repeating circle, already documented in Gauss's observation journals. The only items of interest are small arithmetic slips and corrections.

checkable.asserts: First computed zenith distance is 39°40'17.90" (difference near 0).

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; z,h,f,d=sp.symbols('z h f d'); sp.simplify(sp.expand_trig(sp.sin((d-f)/2)**2*sp.cos(h/2)**2+sp.cos((d+f)/2)**2*sp.sin(h/2)**2 - (1-(sp.sin(f)*sp.sin(d)+sp.cos(f)*sp.cos(d)*sp.cos(h)))/2))
checkable.asserts: Half-angle identity equals sin^2(z/2) from the cosine rule (expected 0).
Sum of seconds and the mean 39°42'38.07".

transcription_corrections: Star name 'ε Cephei' should be β Cephei (Gauss's curly β). RA ≈ 21h26m and δ ≈ 69°44' (1813) fit β Cep at lower culmination. The same applies to 'ι Cephei' on the previous page and 'γ Cepheus' on the next.
The 13.46 and 58.43.45.02 entries are overwritten corrections of 13.44 and 45.00.
